subject: Cloud Computing
title: IaaS Billing Traps
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on IaaS Billing Traps.

hook.text: A startup left a test cluster running over the weekend. Monday's bill: $72,000.

buildup.text: IaaS charges for compute, storage, network transfer, and even idle resources. Every minute counts.

discovery.text: Data transfer out of the cloud is surprisingly expensive. Moving data in is usually free — the hook.

twist.text: Cloud providers make it cheap to put data in and expensive to take it out. That's the lock-in play.

climax.text: Budget alerts and cost anomaly detection exist but most teams enable them after the first shock.

punchline.text: The cloud meter never stops. Set alerts before you get the bill.

quiz.question: Why is data transfer pricing considered a lock-in tactic?
options: Moving data into the cloud is cheap, but moving it out is expensive
Cloud providers charge the same for all data transfers
Data transfer is always free between all cloud providers

details.summary: IaaS billing traps include forgotten running instances, unattached storage volumes, cross-region data transfer fees, and premium support tiers that auto-renew. These hidden costs can multiply cloud bills well beyond the expected compute charges.
details.whyItMatters: Many organizations are shocked by their first cloud bills. Understanding common billing traps prevents waste and keeps cloud adoption financially sustainable.
takeaways: Forgotten instances and unattached volumes accumulate costs
Data transfer fees between regions are often overlooked
Monitoring and alerts are essential for cost control

faq.question: What is the most common IaaS billing surprise?
faq.answer: Forgotten resources that run 24/7 without being used. Developers spin up instances for testing and forget to terminate them. A single forgotten large instance can cost hundreds of dollars per month. Automated shutdown policies eliminate this waste.

faq.question: How can you avoid data transfer cost surprises?
faq.answer: Understand egress pricing before architecting multi-region or hybrid deployments. Use CDNs to reduce origin data transfer, keep cross-region traffic to a minimum, and compress data in transit. Data transfer costs are often the most underestimated line item.
